markdownContent:
# ESQL Production Best Practices & Performance

ESQL compiles to native execution inside the ACE runtime, so clean ESQL processes thousands of messages per second. Follow these **six production habits** (plus extra speed rules) to avoid outages, slow loops, and security leaks.

---

## 6 Habits That Save You in Production

| Habit | Do This in Production | Why It Matters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Loop with `REFERENCE`** | `DECLARE r REFERENCE TO ...Item[1]; WHILE LASTMOVE(r) ... MOVE r NEXTSIBLING REPEAT TYPE NAME;` (or `FOR`) | `Item[i]` and `CARDINALITY(...)` inside a loop walk from index `1` on every iteration ($O(N^2)$ slowdown on large lists!) |
| **2. Default with `COALESCE`** | `COALESCE(InputRoot.JSON.Data.qty, 1)` | Missing fields return `NULL` quietly — deciding what `NULL` means avoids `NULL` math and broken `\|\|` strings |
| **3. Set `Compute mode`** | Pick **`LocalEnvironment And Message`** when editing `OutputLocalEnvironment` | Default `Message` mode silently throws away your HTTP `ReplyStatusCode`, URL, or dynamic MQ destination! |
| **4. Protect `SHARED` data** | Wrap writes to `SHARED` variables inside **`BEGIN ATOMIC ... END;`** | Multiple flow threads share the same `SHARED` memory — unprotected writes corrupt counters and lookup caches |
| **5. Keep secrets out** | Never place passwords, PINs, or full card numbers in `Environment`, logs, or `Trace` | `Environment` travels with the message and can appear in exception dumps, user traces, or monitoring tools |
| **6. Reuse code** | Put shared helpers (`GetLastError`, `MaskCard`) in a **Shared Library** schema (`BROKER SCHEMA <SharedSchemaName>`) | Avoids copy-paste drift; one fix updates every flow cleanly |

---

## Extra Performance Traps to Avoid

| Slow Habit | Fast Replacement | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Repeating `InputRoot.XMLNSC.A.B.C.Field1` 10 times | `DECLARE cRef REFERENCE TO InputRoot.XMLNSC.A.B.C;` then `cRef.Field1` | Navigates the deep path **once** instead of 10 times |
| Calling `CopyEntireMessage()` then replacing the entire body | Call **`CopyMessageHeaders()`** instead | Skips cloning huge input trees you immediately overwrite |
| Building huge strings with `s = s \|\| line` inside a 1,000-step loop | Build message tree elements or use `SELECT` / `FOR` | Repeated string reallocation burns heap memory and CPU |
| Parsing massive XML sections you pass through untouched | Configure **Parser Options -> Opaque Elements** on `MQInput`/`HTTPInput` | ACE keeps opaque subtrees as unparsed text blobs until needed |

---

## Fast Before / After Example (`REFERENCE` Cursor + `COALESCE`)

```esql
-- SLOW: repeated full tree lookup and unguarded nullable field
-- SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.id   = InputRoot.XMLNSC.Payload.Header.Meta.Id;
-- SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.note = 'Note: ' || InputRoot.XMLNSC.Payload.Header.Meta.Note;

-- FAST: single REFERENCE cursor + COALESCE guard
DECLARE metaRef REFERENCE TO InputRoot.XMLNSC.Payload.Header.Meta;

CALL CopyMessageHeaders();
CREATE LASTCHILD OF OutputRoot DOMAIN('JSON');

SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.id   = COALESCE(metaRef.Id, 'MISSING');
SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.note = 'Note: ' || COALESCE(metaRef.Note, 'None');
RETURN TRUE;
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output (When Meta.Note Is Omitted)</summary>

```json
{
  "id": "M-404",
  "note": "Note: None"
}
```

</details>

### Line-by-Line Breakdown

- **`DECLARE metaRef REFERENCE TO InputRoot.XMLNSC.Payload.Header.Meta;`**: Traverses the 4-level XML path **once** and saves the location in `metaRef`.
- **`CALL CopyMessageHeaders();`**: Copies headers cleanly without cloning the incoming `XMLNSC` payload into `OutputRoot`.
- **`COALESCE(metaRef.Id, 'MISSING')` / `COALESCE(metaRef.Note, 'None')`**: Ensures neither `id` nor `'Note: ' || ...` quietly turns into `NULL`.

---

## Recap: Know the Tree, Then Shape It

1. **Read:** Navigate `InputRoot`, `Environment`, and `LocalEnvironment` with exact case-sensitive names and `COALESCE` defaults.
2. **Build:** Create the target output domain (`JSON` / `XMLNSC`), loop with `REFERENCE` + `MOVE` (or `FOR`), and `CAST` / `FORMAT` numbers and dates explicitly.
3. **Control:** Route with `PROPAGATE` (remember `RETURN FALSE;`), look up data safely with parameterized `PASSTHRU`, and fail cleanly with `THROW` + `InputExceptionList`.

---

markdownContent:
# ESQL Common Mistakes & Quick Fixes

Check this diagnostic table whenever a Compute or Filter node produces empty payloads, emits `"Item"` wrappers in JSON, drops HTTP status codes, or fails with `BIP2521E` / `BIP2531E`.

---

## Top 10 ESQL Mistakes & Instant Fixes

| # | Mistake | Symptom / Error | Exact Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | Double quotes for text (`"OK"`) | `"OK"` means a **field name**, so it evaluates to **`NULL`** | Always use **single quotes** for strings (`'OK'`); reserve `"..."` only for special field names like `"Content-Type"` |
| **2** | 0-based array index (`Item[0]`) | Runtime error **`BIP2531E`** | ESQL arrays and `SUBSTRING` positions are **1-based**: `Item[1]` |
| **3** | Writing to `InputRoot` (`SET InputRoot.JSON.Data.a = 1;`) | Runtime error **`BIP2521E`** (*Cannot alter read-only tree*) | Call `CopyEntireMessage()` and modify **`OutputRoot`** instead |
| **4** | Using `InputRoot` in a **`Filter`** or **`Database`** node | Compile error (`InputRoot` undeclared) | **`Filter`** and **`Database`** modules read **`Root`**, NOT `InputRoot`! |
| **5** | Editing `LocalEnvironment` under default `Message` mode | HTTP `ReplyStatusCode` or dynamic target queue is silently ignored | Set node **Properties -> Compute mode** to **`LocalEnvironment And Message`** |
| **6** | Concatenating nullable fields (`a \|\| b`) or comparing `x = NULL` | Output field becomes `NULL` silently; `IF` silently enters `ELSE` (`UNKNOWN`) | Wrap fields in **`COALESCE(field, '')`** and check **`IS NULL`** / **`IS NOT NULL`** |
| **7** | Building JSON arrays without `IDENTITY (JSON.Array)` | JSON comes out as `{"tags": {"Item": "vip"}}` instead of `["vip"]` | Run **`CREATE FIELD OutputRoot.JSON.Data.tags IDENTITY (JSON.Array)tags;`** first |
| **8** | Returning `RETURN TRUE;` after `PROPAGATE` in a loop | Emits an **extra** empty or duplicate message after the batch finishes | Always end with **`RETURN FALSE;`** when `PROPAGATE` already sent all messages |
| **9** | Putting `DECLARE` or `HANDLER` after `SET` / `IF` | Toolkit syntax error in Problems view | Put all `DECLARE` variables first, followed immediately by `DECLARE ... HANDLER`, before any `SET`/`IF`/`CALL` |
| **10** | Wrong field casing (`orderid` vs `orderId`) or `mm` vs `MM` in dates | Field silently evaluates to `NULL`; month prints as minutes | Verify exact case-sensitive JSON/XML field names and use uppercase **`MM`** for month |

---

## Quick Fix Demo: 3 Bugs Fixed in One Snippet

```esql
-- BUGGY VERSION:
-- SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.tag = "VIP";                       -- double quotes -> NULL!
-- SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.first = InputRoot.JSON.Data.x[0];  -- index 0 -> BIP2531E!
-- SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.msg = 'Hi ' || InputRoot.JSON.Data.name; -- NULL if name missing!

-- FIXED VERSION:
CALL CopyMessageHeaders();
CREATE LASTCHILD OF OutputRoot DOMAIN('JSON');

SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.tag   = 'VIP';
SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.first = COALESCE(InputRoot.JSON.Data.x.Item[1], 'N/A');
SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.msg   = 'Hi ' || COALESCE(InputRoot.JSON.Data.name, 'Guest');
RETURN TRUE;
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output (When Input Is {})</summary>

```json
{
  "tag": "VIP",
  "first": "N/A",
  "msg": "Hi Guest"
}
```

</details>

### Line-by-Line Breakdown

- **`'VIP'`**: Single quotes produce the string literal `'VIP'` instead of looking up a field named `VIP`.
- **`InputRoot.JSON.Data.x.Item[1]`**: Starts at 1-based index `[1]` (and follows ACE's `.Item[1]` structure for JSON arrays), guarded with `COALESCE(..., 'N/A')` in case `x` is empty.
- **`'Hi ' || COALESCE(InputRoot.JSON.Data.name, 'Guest')`**: Guarantees `'Hi '` is never wiped out by a `NULL` right-hand operand.

> [!TIP]
> When an ESQL file has a compile error, check the **Problems** tab at the bottom of the ACE Toolkit (or click the red markers on the `.esql` editor scrollbar) to jump straight to the exact offending line.

---

markdownContent:
# ESQL Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

Keep this one-page reference open while writing **Compute**, **Filter**, and **Database** modules in ACE 12 / 13.

---

## 1. Read (Navigate Trees & Safe Defaults)

| Need | Exact ESQL Snippet |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Root trees in Compute vs Filter/DB** | `InputRoot` / `OutputRoot` (`Compute`) · `Root` (`Filter` / `Database`) |
| **First / Last element (1-based!)** | `InputRoot.XMLNSC.Order.Item[1]` / `InputRoot.XMLNSC.Order.Item[<]` |
| **Count / Presence check** | `CARDINALITY(InputRoot.XMLNSC.Order.Item[])` / `EXISTS(InputRoot.JSON.Data.email[])` |
| **XML Attribute / Root Tag / Namespace** | `Order.(XMLNSC.Attribute)id` · `FIELDNAME(InputBody.*[1])` · `DECLARE ns NAMESPACE '<NamespaceUri>';` |
| **Safe `NULL` fallback / blank check** | `COALESCE(field, 'default')` · `COALESCE(field, '') = ''` · `field IS NOT NULL` |
| **Declare variables & modifiers** | `DECLARE amt DECIMAL 10.50;` · `CONSTANT` · `EXTERNAL` · `SHARED ROW` (write in `BEGIN ATOMIC`) |
| **Fast tree cursor (`REFERENCE` + `MOVE`)** | `DECLARE r REFERENCE TO ...Item[1]; WHILE LASTMOVE(r) DO ... MOVE r NEXTSIBLING REPEAT TYPE NAME; END WHILE;` |

---

## 2. Build (Construct Domains, Arrays, Strings, Casts & Dates)

| Need | Exact ESQL Snippet |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Copy headers vs full message** | `CALL CopyMessageHeaders();` / `CALL CopyEntireMessage();` |
| **Create body domain** | `CREATE LASTCHILD OF OutputRoot DOMAIN('JSON');` (or `'XMLNSC'`) |
| **Create JSON array** | `CREATE FIELD OutputRoot.JSON.Data.tags IDENTITY (JSON.Array)tags;` |
| **Create / Append / Prepend / Delete** | `CREATE FIELD` · `CREATE LASTCHILD OF p AS r NAME 'Item';` · `CREATE FIRSTCHILD` · `DELETE FIELD` |
| **Move subtree without copying** | `DETACH ref; ATTACH ref TO targetRef AS LASTCHILD;` |
| **In-memory `SELECT`, `ITEM`, `THE`** | `THE(SELECT ITEM C.name FROM InputRoot.JSON.Data.customers.Item[] AS C WHERE C.id = '1001')` |
| **String slicing & masking** | `SUBSTRING('ORD-2026' FROM 5 FOR 4)` · `UPPER(TRIM(' egp '))` · `LEFT(c,6) \|\| REPLICATE('*', n-10) \|\| RIGHT(c,4)` |
| **Safe type cast & rounding** | `CAST(val AS INTEGER DEFAULT 0)` · `ROUND(amt, 2)` · `CAST(blobVar AS CHARACTER CCSID 1208)` |
| **Parse & format dates (`''T''`)** | `CAST(d AS CHARACTER FORMAT 'yyyy-MM-dd')` · `CAST(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS CHARACTER FORMAT 'yyyy-MM-dd''T''HH:mm:ss')` |
| **Tree <-> `BLOB` (`ASBITSTREAM`/`PARSE`)** | `ASBITSTREAM(InputRoot.XMLNSC OPTIONS FolderBitStream ENCODING 546 CCSID 1208)` |

---

## 3. Control, Errors & Best Practices

| Need | Exact ESQL Snippet |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`IF` / `CASE` / `FOR` / `LOOP`** | `IF ... ELSEIF ... ELSE END IF;` · `FOR x AS ...[] DO ... END FOR;` · `L1: LOOP ... LEAVE L1; END LOOP L1;` |
| **`Environment` vs `LocalEnvironment`** | `Environment.Variables.x` (flow-wide) · `OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.HTTP.ReplyStatusCode = 404;` *(set Compute mode!)* |
| **Split / route multiple outputs** | `PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL 'out1';` *(end `Main()` with `RETURN FALSE;`!)* · `DELETE NONE` keeps `OutputRoot` |
| **Set MQ / HTTP headers** | `SET OutputRoot.MQMD.CorrelId = InputRoot.MQMD.MsgId;` · `OutputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."Content-Type"` |
| **Database lookup (`PASSTHRU`)** | `SET Environment.Variables.cust[] = PASSTHRU('SELECT NAME FROM <TableName> WHERE CUST_ID = ?', id);` |
| **Raise error (`THROW`)** | `THROW USER EXCEPTION MESSAGE 2951 VALUES('email is required');` |
| **Inline error handler** | `DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR SQLSTATE LIKE '%' BEGIN SET err = SQLSTATE; END;` *(top of `BEGIN`!)* |
| **Walk `InputExceptionList` (Catch)** | `DECLARE e REFERENCE TO InputExceptionList.*[1]; WHILE LASTMOVE(e) DO ... MOVE e LASTCHILD; END WHILE;` |
| **Reuse functions across flows** | Put `CREATE FUNCTION` / `CREATE PROCEDURE` in Shared Library schema + import with `PATH <SharedSchemaName>;` |

---

# mqsiprofile & the ACE Command Console

Every ACE CLI command (`mqsilist`, `mqsistart`, `mqsideploy`, `ibmint`) only works **after** your shell loads IBM's `mqsiprofile` paths and environment variables.

---

## Easiest Way on Windows

Open the Start Menu -> **IBM App Connect Enterprise 12.x -> IBM App Connect Enterprise Console**.
It opens a shell with `mqsiprofile` **already loaded automatically**.

---

## Using Your Own Terminal (CMD / Bash / Git Bash)

```bat
REM Windows CMD (runs once per open window)
"C:\Program Files\IBM\ACE\12.0.x.x\server\bin\mqsiprofile.cmd"
```

```bash
# Linux / Mac / Container shell (notice the dot + space at the start!)
. /opt/ibm/ace-12/server/bin/mqsiprofile
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Verify Environment Loaded</summary>

```text
MQSI_VERSION 12.0.11.0
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

> [!TIP]
> Notice the leading `. ` *(dot space)* on Linux! Running `/opt/ibm/.../mqsiprofile` without `. ` runs inside a child shell and disappears right after — `. ` loads variables into **your current terminal**.

---

# Fix: 'mqsi' Is Not Recognized as a Command

If typing `mqsilist` gives `'mqsilist' is not recognized as an internal or external command` (Windows) or `command not found` (Linux), nothing is broken — **`mqsiprofile` just isn't loaded in that terminal tab yet**.

---

## 30-Second Fix

| Your Shell | Fix Command |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Windows Start Menu** | Close regular CMD and open **IBM App Connect Enterprise Console** |
| **Regular Windows CMD** | `"C:\Program Files\IBM\ACE\12.0.x.x\server\bin\mqsiprofile.cmd"` |
| **PowerShell** | PowerShell cannot source `.cmd` directly — launch CMD first: `cmd /k "C:\Program Files\IBM\ACE\12.0.x.x\server\bin\mqsiprofile.cmd"` |
| **Linux / Docker / WSL** | `. /opt/ibm/ace-12/server/bin/mqsiprofile` |

---

## Test That It Worked

```bash
mqsilist -v
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output Once Fixed</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

> [!WARNING]
> Do **not** manually hack Windows global System `PATH` to mix two different ACE versions (like v11 and v12). Using the Start Menu Console or `mqsiprofile` keeps every terminal clean.

---

# Real Session Startup Walkthrough (MQ + ACE)

Opening your laptop after a reboot? Here is the exact **order of commands** to verify IBM MQ and ACE are healthy and start your Integration Node.

---

## Always Start in This Order: **MQ First -> ACE Second**

```bash
# 1. Check existing Queue Managers
dspmq

# 2. Start your Queue Manager (e.g., <QueueManagerName>)
strmqm <QueueManagerName>

# 3. Check ACE Integration Nodes
mqsilist

# 4. Start your Integration Node (starts managed servers inside it too!)
mqsistart <IntegrationNodeName>

# 5. Confirm everything reports 'running'
mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Clean Startup Output</summary>

```text
QMNAME(<QueueManagerName>)                                             STATUS(Running)
BIP8096I: Successful command initiation, check the system log to ensure that the component started without problem and that it continues to run without problem.
BIP1284I: Integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' on integration node '<IntegrationNodeName>' is running.
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Quick Verification After Starting

1. Run `mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName>` -> look for `is running`.
2. Open ACE Toolkit -> **Integration Explorer** -> right-click **Integration Nodes** -> **Refresh**.
3. Drop a test message with `amqsput <InputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>` or **Flow Exerciser**.

> [!TIP]
> Shutting down at the end of the day? Reverse the order: **`mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName>` first**, then **`endmqm <QueueManagerName>`** so ACE finishes inflight queue transactions cleanly!

---

markdownContent:
# mqsilist: Inspect Nodes, Servers & Flows

**`mqsilist`** is your status camera for ACE — run it with no flags for nodes, add a node name for servers, or drill all the way down to running flows.

![Integration Explorer panel matching the node, server, and deployed resource tree shown by mqsilist](/images/ace/integration-explorer-nodes.png)

---

## Syntax Levels (Zoom In Deeper)

| Command | What It Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mqsilist` | Every Integration Node on this PC + linked Queue Manager + status |
| `mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName>` | All Integration Servers (`<IntegrationServerName>`) running inside node `<IntegrationNodeName>` |
| `mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>` | All Applications, Libraries, and Policies deployed on server `<IntegrationServerName>` |
| `mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -k <ApplicationName> -d 2` | Deep view (`-d 2`) of every flow, status, and endpoints inside `<ApplicationName>` |

---

## Fast Example

```bash
mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP1275I: Application '<ApplicationName>' on integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' is running.
BIP1284I: Integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' on integration node '<IntegrationNodeName>' is running.
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

> [!TIP]
> Running an **Independent Integration Server**? Point `mqsilist` directly at its HTTP admin port: `mqsilist -i localhost -p 7600 -d 2`!

---

# mqsicreatebroker & mqsideletebroker

Use **`mqsicreatebroker`** to create an Integration Node on your machine, and **`mqsideletebroker`** to remove it cleanly when no longer needed.

---

## Create an Integration Node

```bash
# Without MQ link (HTTP / File flows only)
mqsicreatebroker <IntegrationNodeName>

# Linked to local IBM MQ Queue Manager <QueueManagerName> (recommended for MQ flows)
mqsicreatebroker <IntegrationNodeName> -q <QueueManagerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Delete an Integration Node (Must Be Stopped First!)

```bash
mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName>
mqsideletebroker <IntegrationNodeName>
```

- Notice deleting an Integration Node deletes its managed servers and deployed flows inside it — add **`-w`** (`mqsideletebroker <IntegrationNodeName> -w`) if you also want to clean its workpath/registry files cleanly.

> [!NOTE]
> Remember IBM MQ Queue Manager `<QueueManagerName>` must **already exist** before linking it with `-q <QueueManagerName>`, or creation succeeds with a warning and startup later fails until `<QueueManagerName>` is created.

---

# mqsistart & mqsistop (Integration Nodes)

Use **`mqsistart`** and **`mqsistop`** to bring an entire Integration Node (and all its configured Integration Servers) online or offline.

---

## Syntax & Example

```bash
# Start node <IntegrationNodeName> (also starts linked QMGR if needed)
mqsistart <IntegrationNodeName>

# Stop gracefully (waits for active flows to finish)
mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName>

# Emergency force stop (ONLY if normal stop hangs!)
mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName> -i
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Start Output</summary>

```text
BIP8096I: Successful command initiation, check the system log to ensure that the component started without problem and that it continues to run without problem.
```

</details>

---

## Good to Know

| Flag / Behavior | What Happens |
| :--- | :--- |
| Normal **`mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName>`** | Lets in-flight messages commit cleanly before shutting down servers |
| Immediate **`mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName> -i`** | Kills server processes immediately without waiting — use only if a flow is deadlocked |
| **Toolkit shortcut** | You can also right-click your Node in **Integration Explorer -> Start / Stop** |

---

markdownContent:
# Change Properties Live (mqsichangeproperties)

Use **`mqsichangeproperties`** to update server or node settings from the command line — notice you always pass the Node (`<IntegrationNodeName>`), optional Server (`-e <IntegrationServerName>`), component (`-o`), property name (`-n`), and new value (`-v`).

---

## Syntax & Fast Examples

```bash
# Change server <IntegrationServerName> embedded HTTP port to 7808
mqsichangeproperties <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -o HTTPConnector -n port -v 7808

# Increase JVM max heap to 1 GB on server <IntegrationServerName>
mqsichangeproperties <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -o ComIbmJVMManager -n jvmMaxHeapSize -v 1073741824

# Restart server so changes take effect cleanly
mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> && mqsistart <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Key Flags Cheat Table

| Flag | Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`-e <IntegrationServerName>`** | Target Integration Server (omit for Node-wide) | `-e <IntegrationServerName>` |
| **`-o`** | Object/component name | `-o HTTPConnector`, `-o ComIbmJVMManager` |
| **`-n`** | Property name | `-n port` |
| **`-v`** | New value | `-v 7808` |

> [!NOTE]
> Many property updates (especially `ComIbmJVMManager` and listener ports) require restarting the Integration Server (or Node) before taking effect.

---

markdownContent:
# Managed Integration Servers (Overview)

An **Integration Server** *(called Execution Group in older versions)* is an isolated OS worker process (`DataFlowEngine`) managed by an Integration Node.

![Integration Explorer showing Integration Servers running under an Integration Node](/images/ace/integration-explorer-nodes.png)

---

## Why Use Multiple Servers on One Node?

| Benefit | Real Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Crash Isolation** | If `<Server1Name>` runs out of memory, `<Server2Name>` stays completely unaffected |
| **Independent Restarts** | Restart or deploy to `<IntegrationServerName>` without dropping HTTP traffic on `<Server2Name>` |
| **Separate JVM & HTTP Ports** | Give `<IntegrationServerName>` port `7800` + 512MB RAM and `<Server2Name>` port `7801` + 2GB RAM |

---

## Managed vs. Independent Server

- **Managed Server** *(created inside a Node)*: Controlled via `mqsicreateexecutiongroup`, `mqsideploy NODE -e <IntegrationServerName>`, etc.
- **Independent Server** *(no Integration Node)*: Created in a folder via `mqsicreateworkdir` and started directly via `IntegrationServer`.

---

markdownContent:
# mqsicreateexecutiongroup: Add a Server

Use **`mqsicreateexecutiongroup`** to add a new Integration Server inside an already-running Integration Node (such as `<IntegrationNodeName>`).

---

## Syntax & Example

```bash
# Make sure node <IntegrationNodeName> is running first!
mqsistart <IntegrationNodeName>

# Create server <IntegrationServerName> inside <IntegrationNodeName>
mqsicreateexecutiongroup <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Good to Know

- Notice the Integration Node **must be running** before calling `mqsicreateexecutiongroup`.
- Verify immediately with `mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName>` — `<IntegrationServerName>` automatically starts as part of creation!
- Need to point directly to a remote Node? Pass host/port or a `.broker` file with `-i` and `-p`.

---

markdownContent:
# Start & Stop a Managed Integration Server

You don't have to reboot the entire Integration Node just to restart one server — pass **`-e <ServerName>`** to `mqsistop` and `mqsistart`.

---

## Syntax & Example

```bash
# Stop ONLY server <IntegrationServerName> inside node <IntegrationNodeName> (other servers keep running!)
mqsistop <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>

# Start ONLY server <IntegrationServerName> back up
mqsistart <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP1285I: Integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' on integration node '<IntegrationNodeName>' has been stopped.
BIP1284I: Integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' on integration node '<IntegrationNodeName>' is running.
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

> [!TIP]
> Verify right away with `mqsilist <IntegrationNodeName>` — if a server fails to come back up, check `mqsicvp` or Windows Event Viewer / syslog for port conflicts (`HTTPConnector` port already bound).

---

# mqsideleteexecutiongroup: Remove a Server

Use **`mqsideleteexecutiongroup`** to remove an unused Integration Server from an Integration Node.

---

## Syntax & Example

```bash
# Integration Node <IntegrationNodeName> must be running!
mqsideleteexecutiongroup <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

> [!WARNING]
> Deleting a server **removes all Applications, Libraries, and Policies deployed inside it** cleanly without confirmation prompts — double check the `-e` name first! Add **`-w 60000`** (milliseconds) if a busy server needs extra time to stop gracefully before deletion.

markdownContent:
# Independent Integration Server (mqsicreateworkdir)

In ACE 12, you don't even have to create an Integration Node for local testing or Docker containers! You can create a folder with **`mqsicreateworkdir`** and launch **`IntegrationServer`** directly.

---

## Step 1: Create the Server Work Directory

```bash
mqsicreateworkdir <WorkDirPath>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>What Gets Created Inside <WorkDirPath></summary>

```text
mqsicreateworkdir: Copying sample server.conf.yaml to <WorkDirPath>
  config/
  overrides/
  run/          <-- Drop .bar files or deployed apps here!
  server.conf.yaml
```

</details>

---

## Step 2: Start the Independent Server

```bash
IntegrationServer --name <IntegrationServerName> --work-dir <WorkDirPath>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Console Startup Log</summary>

```text
BIP1990I: Integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' starting initialization; version '12.0.11.0'
BIP2866I: IBM App Connect Enterprise administration security is inactive.
BIP1991I: Integration server has finished initialization.
```

</details>

---

## When to Pick Independent vs. Node-Managed

| Feature | Independent Server | Node-Managed Server |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Needs `mqsicreatebroker`? | **No!** | Yes |
| Docker / Kubernetes ready? | **Yes — standard pattern** | Rarely used in containers |
| Connect in Toolkit | **Integration Explorer -> Right-click Integration Servers -> Connect** (`localhost:7600`) | Connects automatically under Integration Node |

> [!TIP]
> Notice the process stays attached in your terminal — press **Ctrl+C** to shut it down cleanly when you're done developing!

---

title: Configure Servers with server.conf.yaml
shortDescription: Edit server.conf.yaml to set REST admin ports, HTTP listener ports, default Queue Manager, and JVM heap cleanly.
markdownContent:
# Configure Servers with server.conf.yaml

Every ACE 12 Integration Server is configured through a clean, readable YAML file called **`server.conf.yaml`** (or `overrides/server.conf.yaml`).

---

## Essential Settings Beginners Change Most

```yaml
# Located in <work-dir>/server.conf.yaml
restAdminListener:
  port: 7600                  # Web UI & mqsideploy / Toolkit admin port

defaultQueueManager: '<QueueManagerName>'  # Default local MQ Queue Manager if node doesn't specify one

ResourceManagers:
  HTTPConnector:
    ListenerPort: 7800        # Default port for HTTPInput nodes
  JVM:
    jvmMaxHeapSize: 536870912 # 512 MB max JVM heap
```

---

## 2 Strict YAML Rules (Don't Break Startup!)

1. **Always use SPACES (2 spaces), NEVER TAB characters!** A single Tab in YAML crashes server startup with a YAML parser error.
2. Put custom overrides inside **`overrides/server.conf.yaml`** (only the 3–4 lines you change) — IBM preserves `overrides/` across fixpack upgrades and overrides base settings cleanly!

> [!TIP]
> Remember to restart your `IntegrationServer` after editing `server.conf.yaml` for changes to take effect.

---

# BAR Packaging (Toolkit & ibmint package)

A **BAR (Broker Archive)** is a `.bar` zip package containing compiled flows, ESQL, schemas, and maps ready for deployment.

![Toolkit BAR Editor Prepare tab selecting Applications and Shared Libraries to build a .bar file](/images/ace/bar-editor-prepare.png)

---

## Option A: Build in Toolkit (GUI)

1. Right-click anywhere in **Application Development -> New -> BAR file**.
2. Type a name like `<BarFileName>.bar` and click **Finish**.
3. Check the Applications / Shared Libraries / Policy Projects to include, then click **Build and Save**.

---

## Option B: Build in Terminal / CI/CD (`ibmint package`)

```bash
ibmint package --input-path <WorkspacePath> --output-bar-file <BarFilePath> --project <ApplicationName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP15201I: Packaging project '<ApplicationName>' into bar file '<BarFilePath>'.
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

> [!TIP]
> Building in CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins/GitHub Actions) without launching the Eclipse GUI? **`ibmint package`** (ACE v12+) compiles everything directly from Git source cleanly with zero X11 display needed!

---

markdownContent:
# Inspect & Override BARs (mqsireadbar & Override)

Never open `.bar` binaries in Notepad! Use **`mqsireadbar`** to list every configurable queue name, URL, or instance count inside a `.bar`, and **`mqsiapplybaroverride`** to swap values between DEV and PROD.

![BAR Editor Manage & Configure tab showing configurable node properties inside a BAR file](/images/ace/bar-editor-manage-mq.png)

---

## Step 1: See Every Configurable Key Inside the BAR

```bash
mqsireadbar -b <BarFilePath> -r
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP1052I: Reading Broker Archive using runtime integration node or server.
<ApplicationName>.appzip:
  <MessageFlowName>.msgflow:
    MQInput#queueName = <InputQueueName>
    MQOutput#queueName = <OutputQueueName>
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Step 2: Override Values for UAT/PROD

Create `<OverridePropertiesFile>.properties`:
```properties
<MessageFlowName>#MQInput.queueName=UAT.<InputQueueName>
<MessageFlowName>#MQOutput.queueName=UAT.<OutputQueueName>
```

Then stamp a UAT-ready copy of the BAR:
```bash
mqsiapplybaroverride -b <BarFileName>.bar -p <OverridePropertiesFile>.properties -o <TargetEnvBarFile>.bar
```

> [!TIP]
> Notice for **MQ connection endpoints**, using an **`MQEndpoint` Policy Project** is cleaner than per-node BAR overrides — use `mqsiapplybaroverride` primarily for queue names, additional thread instances, or HTTP URL paths.

---

title: mqsideploy: Deploy, List & Clean Flows
shortDescription: Deploy a .bar file from the CLI onto a managed server or an Independent Integration Server (or delete deployed apps).

Deploy to an Independent Integration Server (via REST port 7600)
markdownContent:
# mqsideploy: Deploy, List & Clean Flows

**`mqsideploy`** pushes a `.bar` archive onto a running Integration Server (or removes existing apps cleanly).

![Deploy BAR wizard in the Toolkit showing target Integration Server selection](/images/ace/deploy-select-integration-server.png)

---

## Common Deployment Commands

```bash
# Deploy to a Managed Server (Node <IntegrationNodeName>, server <IntegrationServerName>)
mqsideploy <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -a <BarFilePath>

# Full clean deploy (-m deletes old apps not in this BAR!)
mqsideploy <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -a <BarFilePath> -m

# Deploy to an Independent Integration Server (via REST port 7600)
mqsideploy -i localhost -p 7600 -a <BarFilePath>

# Remove an application by name (-d)
mqsideploy <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -d <ApplicationName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP1039I: Deploying BAR file '<BarFilePath>' to integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' ...
BIP9332I: Application '<ApplicationName>' has been created or updated successfully.
BIP1092I: The integration node successfully processed the deployment request.
```

</details>

---

> [!WARNING]
> **Careful with `-m` (`complete deployment`)!** Adding `-m` deletes **everything else** already deployed on that Integration Server (`<IntegrationServerName>`) that is not inside your `.bar` file. Omit `-m` for normal incremental app deploys.

---

title: mqsistartmsgflow & mqsistopmsgflow
shortDescription: Pause or resume individual Message Flows or entire Applications without stopping the Integration Server.

markdownContent:
# mqsistartmsgflow & mqsistopmsgflow

Need to pause one buggy flow during maintenance while keeping other flows on the same server running? Use **`mqsistopmsgflow`** and **`mqsistartmsgflow`**.

---

## Syntax & Examples

```bash
# Stop ONE specific message flow inside Application <ApplicationName>
mqsistopmsgflow <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -k <ApplicationName> -m <MessageFlowName>

# Stop the ENTIRE Application <ApplicationName> (all flows inside it)
mqsistopmsgflow <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -k <ApplicationName>

# Start it back up cleanly
mqsistartmsgflow <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName> -k <ApplicationName> -m <MessageFlowName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP1276I: Message flow '<MessageFlowName>' on integration server '<IntegrationServerName>' has been stopped.
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Same Action on an Independent Server

Replace `<IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>` with `-i localhost -p 7600`:
```bash
mqsistopmsgflow -i localhost -p 7600 -k <ApplicationName> -m <MessageFlowName>
```

> [!TIP]
> Notice stopping `<ApplicationName>` pauses its triggers (`MQInput` stops reading `<InputQueueName>`, `HTTPInput` returns `503`), letting messages build safely in IBM MQ until you call `mqsistartmsgflow`.

---

title: mqsireload: Restart Execution Groups & Reload Policies

markdownContent:
# mqsireload: Restart Execution Groups & Reload Policies

After running **`mqsisetdbparms`** (setting database or MQ credentials) or updating security profiles, an Integration Server only picks up the new credentials once reloaded with **`mqsireload`**.

---

## Syntax & Fast Example

```bash
# 1. Set or update ODBC database credentials on node <IntegrationNodeName>
mqsisetdbparms <IntegrationNodeName> -n odbc::<DSN_Name> -u <UserName> -p <Password>

# 2. Reload server <IntegrationServerName> immediately so it picks up new credentials
mqsireload <IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>

# Or reload ALL managed servers on node <IntegrationNodeName>
mqsireload <IntegrationNodeName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

> [!NOTE]
> `mqsireload` briefly stops and starts the Integration Server process (similar to `mqsistop -e` + `mqsistart -e` in a single atomic command). Use `-i` for immediate restart if an active flow is stuck.
> Need full SQL Server ODBC credential & `mqsicvp` setup? See **[SQL Server Credentials & mqsicvp Test →](#topic-252)**.

---

title: mqsichangetrace: Turn User & Service Trace On/Off
shortDescription: Capture step-by-step execution trace logs when Flow Exerciser isn't available (or in headless test/UAT servers).
searchableTerms: mqsichangetrace: Turn User & Service Trace On/Off
1. Turn User Trace ON (debug level, 20MB buffer) for server <IntegrationServerName>
3. Turn User Trace OFF right away!
cheatSheetText: Trace Type Flag What It Records Use When... User Trace -u Every node entry/exit, ESQL statement, route match, and error 95% of flow & ESQL debugging Service Trace -t Deep internal C++/IBM Support engine logs Requested by IBM Support (huge logs, slow!)
markdownContent:
# mqsichangetrace: Turn User & Service Trace On/Off

When a flow fails silently or behaves unexpectedly on a remote server, turn on **User Trace (`-u`)** temporarily, reproduce the bug **once**, and then **turn trace OFF (`-l none`)** immediately.

---

## User Trace vs. Service Trace

| Trace Type | Flag | What It Records | Use When... |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **User Trace** | `-u` | Every node entry/exit, ESQL statement, route match, and error | **95% of flow & ESQL debugging** |
| **Service Trace** | `-t` | Deep internal C++/IBM Support engine logs | Requested by IBM Support (huge logs, slow!) |

---

## Fast Copy-Paste Debug Workflow

```bash
# 1. Turn User Trace ON (debug level, 20MB buffer) for server <IntegrationServerName>
mqsichangetrace <IntegrationNodeName> -u -e <IntegrationServerName> -l debug -c 20480 -r

# 2. >>> Send 1 test message now! <<<

# 3. Turn User Trace OFF right away!
mqsichangetrace <IntegrationNodeName> -u -e <IntegrationServerName> -l none
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

> [!WARNING]
> **NEVER forget step 3 (`-l none`)!** Leaving `-l debug` trace running in production slashes throughput by 50–80% and fills trace buffers rapidly. On an Independent Server, use `-w <WorkDirPath>` instead of `<IntegrationNodeName> -e <IntegrationServerName>`.

---

title: mqsireadlog & mqsiformatlog: Read Trace Logs

markdownContent:
# mqsireadlog & mqsiformatlog: Read Trace Logs

ACE stores trace logs internally in compact binary/XML format. To actually read them like plain English, run **two quick commands back-to-back**: `mqsireadlog` -> `mqsiformatlog`.

---

## Two-Step Read Workflow

```bash
# 1. Export internal User Trace (-u) buffer to XML file
mqsireadlog <IntegrationNodeName> -u -e <IntegrationServerName> -o <TraceXmlPath>

# 2. Format that XML into readable plain text
```

# runmqsc: The Interactive MQ Admin Shell

IBM MQ divides commands in two: **OS shell commands** (like `crtmqm`, `strmqm`, `dspmq`) and **MQSC commands** typed **inside `runmqsc`** (like `DEFINE QLOCAL`, `DISPLAY QSTATUS`).

---

## Mode 1: Interactive Shell

```bash
runmqsc <QueueManagerName>
```

Once inside `Starting MQSC for queue manager <QueueManagerName>.`, type MQSC commands directly, and type **`END`** to exit back to CMD/Bash:

```text
DEFINE QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') REPLACE
DISPLAY QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>')
END
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
5724-H72 (C) Copyright IBM Corp. 1994, 2024.
Starting MQSC for queue manager <QueueManagerName>.

     1 : DEFINE QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') REPLACE
AMQ8006I: IBM MQ queue created.
     2 : END
One MQSC command read.
No commands have a syntax error.
```

</details>

---

## Mode 2: Quick Script / Pipe One-Liner

Skip typing `END` manually by piping commands into `runmqsc`:

```bash
echo DISPLAY QLOCAL(*) | runmqsc <QueueManagerName>
```

> [!TIP]
> Notice **MQSC converts unquoted names to UPPERCASE automatically!** Always wrap queue names in **single quotes (`'<InputQueueName>'`)** if your queue or channel uses lowercase or dots!

# MQ Object Types (QMGR, Queue, Channel, Listener)

Every IBM MQ environment — from a developer laptop to a bank cluster — runs on **4 core objects**.

---

## How the 4 Objects Work Together

| Object | Simple Job | Real Example | When Needed? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Queue Manager (`QMGR`)** | The MQ server container | `<QueueManagerName>` | Always (hosts everything below) |
| **Queue (`QLOCAL`)** | Mailbox storing messages | `<InputQueueName>`, `<OutputQueueName>` | Always (where ACE reads/writes) |
| **Listener (`LISTENER`)** | Opens a TCP/IP network port | `<ListenerName>` on port `1414` | Whenever apps or ACE connect **remotely** (`CLIENT` mode) |
| **Channel (`SVRCONN`)** | Network doorway for remote apps | `<ChannelName>` | Whenever apps or ACE connect **remotely** (`CLIENT` mode) |

---

> [!NOTE]
> Running ACE and MQ **on the same PC in Local Bindings mode**? You only need a **Queue Manager** and **Local Queues** — Listener and `SVRCONN` channel are only required for TCP client connections or **MQ Explorer** remote UI access!

# crtmqm: Create a Queue Manager

**`crtmqm`** creates a brand-new Queue Manager directory, recovery logs, and system queues (`SYSTEM.*`).

---

## Syntax & Example

```bash
# Create Queue Manager <QueueManagerName> and mark it as this PC's default (-q)
crtmqm -q <QueueManagerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
IBM MQ queue manager created.
Directory 'C:\ProgramData\IBM\MQ\qmgrs\<QueueManagerName>' created.
The queue manager is associated with installation 'Installation1'.
Creating or replacing default objects for queue manager '<QueueManagerName>'.
Default objects statistics : 84 created. 0 replaced. 0 failed.
Completing setup.
Setup completed.
```

</details>

## Useful Flags

| Flag | Meaning | Best For |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`-q`** | Sets this as the default QMGR (`strmqm`, `runmqsc` work without typing a name) | Single-QMGR dev laptops |
| **`-lc`** | Circular logging *(default)* — automatically reuses log files so disk stays fixed | Local dev & standard messaging |
| **`-ll`** | Linear logging — keeps archival logs for point-in-time media recovery | High-compliance production |

# strmqm, endmqm & dltmqm: Start, Stop & Delete

Manage the full lifecycle of an IBM MQ Queue Manager from your OS shell (`CMD` or `Bash`, not inside `runmqsc`).

---

## Start, Stop & Delete Commands

```bash
# 1. Start Queue Manager <QueueManagerName>
strmqm <QueueManagerName>

# 2. Controlled stop (waits for active apps to disconnect)
endmqm <QueueManagerName>

# 3. Wait until stop completes (-w) OR immediate stop (-i) if an app stays connected
endmqm -w -i <QueueManagerName>

# 4. Permanently delete a STOPPED Queue Manager (and all its queues/messages!)
dltmqm <QueueManagerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
IBM MQ queue manager '<QueueManagerName>' starting.
IBM MQ queue manager '<QueueManagerName>' started using V9.4.0.0.
```

</details>

---

> [!WARNING]
> Running `endmqm <QueueManagerName>` without `-i` can hang for minutes if **ACE** still holds an open connection! Always run **`mqsistop <Node>` first**, then **`endmqm -w <QueueManagerName>`** (or `endmqm -i <QueueManagerName>` in dev).

markdownContent:
# DEFINE QLOCAL: Create a Local Queue

Every queue your ACE `MQInput` or `MQOutput` node names **must exist on the Queue Manager** first. You can create queues either in **MQ Explorer** or with one command in **`runmqsc`**.

![IBM MQ Explorer wizard creating a New Local Queue](/images/ace/mq-explorer-create-local-queue.png)

---

## Create Queues via CLI (`runmqsc`)

```bash
runmqsc <QueueManagerName>
```

Inside `runmqsc`:

```text
DEFINE QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>')  DESCR('Orders inbound queue')  DEFPSIST(YES) MAXDEPTH(50000) REPLACE
DEFINE QLOCAL('<OutputQueueName>') DESCR('Orders outbound queue') DEFPSIST(YES) MAXDEPTH(50000) REPLACE
END
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
AMQ8006I: IBM MQ queue created.
AMQ8006I: IBM MQ queue created.
```

</details>

---

## Key Queue Options Explained

| Attribute | Recommended Setting | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`DEFPSIST(YES)`** | Persistent by default | Messages survive an MQ restart if sender uses default persistence |
| **`MAXDEPTH(50000)`** | Max queued messages (default `5000`) | Prevents fast producers filling a small `5000` dev queue (`MQRC 2053`) |
| **`REPLACE`** | Updates properties safely if already exists | Makes scripts idempotent (`run` cleanly twice!) |

> [!TIP]
> Queue names are **case-sensitive**: `'<InputQueueName>'` and `'in.q'` are completely different queues in IBM MQ! Stick to uppercase letters and dots (`APP.<InputQueueName>`) cleanly across MQ and ACE.

---

# DISPLAY QUEUE & ALTER QLOCAL: Inspect & Edit

Use **`DISPLAY QLOCAL`** to list queues or read settings (including how many messages are currently sitting inside with **`CURDEPTH`**), and **`ALTER QLOCAL`** to change properties on the fly.

---

## Common Inspect & Edit Commands (Inside `runmqsc`)

```text
* List all non-system user queues cleanly (skip SYSTEM.* clutter)
DISPLAY QLOCAL(*) WHERE(NAME NS 'SYSTEM.') CURDEPTH MAXDEPTH

* Check every setting on <InputQueueName>
DISPLAY QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') ALL

* Increase MAXDEPTH to 100,000 without losing messages
ALTER QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') MAXDEPTH(100000)

* Temporarily block producers from putting new messages (GET still allowed!)
ALTER QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') PUT(DISABLED)
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
AMQ8409I: Display Queue details.
   QUEUE(<InputQueueName>)                             TYPE(QLOCAL)
   CURDEPTH(3)                             MAXDEPTH(50000)
AMQ8409I: Display Queue details.
   QUEUE(<OutputQueueName>)                            TYPE(QLOCAL)
   CURDEPTH(0)                             MAXDEPTH(50000)
```

</details>

---

> [!TIP]
> `PUT(DISABLED)` is super handy during maintenance: callers stop putting new messages on `<InputQueueName>`, while your ACE flow finishes draining the remaining `CURDEPTH` safely! Set `PUT(ENABLED)` when done.

---

# CLEAR QLOCAL & DELETE QLOCAL: Empty or Remove

Need to wipe 500 bad test messages out of `<InputQueueName>` during dev? Use **`CLEAR QLOCAL`** inside `runmqsc`. Want to remove the queue definition altogether? Use **`DELETE QLOCAL`**.

---

## Commands (Inside `runmqsc <QueueManagerName>`)

```text
* Empty all messages inside <InputQueueName> (queue definition stays!)
CLEAR QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>')

* Permanently remove queue <QueueName> (must be empty first!)
DELETE QLOCAL('<QueueName>')

* Delete queue EVEN if messages still sit inside (USE CAREFULLY!)
DELETE QLOCAL('<QueueName>') PURGE
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
AMQ8022I: IBM MQ queue cleared.
```

</details>

---

> [!WARNING]
> Getting **`AMQ8148S: IBM MQ object in use`** when running `CLEAR QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>')`? That means an active app (usually your **ACE `MQInput` flow!**) has the queue open for reading (`IPPROCS > 0`). Stop the flow first (`mqsistopmsgflow ...`) or read messages cleanly with `amqsget`, then clear!

# DISPLAY QSTATUS: Who Is Connected & Queue Depth

Messages piling up in `<InputQueueName>`? Run **`DISPLAY QSTATUS`** inside `runmqsc` to see **if ACE is actually listening** and **which exact process holds the queue open**.

![IBM MQ Explorer Queues panel showing Current queue depth and Open input/output counts](/images/ace/mq-explorer-queues-depth.png)

---

## Check Live Queue State (`runmqsc`)

```text
* Check queue depth, open readers (IPPROCS), open writers (OPPROCS), oldest msg age
DISPLAY QSTATUS('<InputQueueName>') CURDEPTH IPPROCS OPPROCS MSGAGE

* See the EXACT app name and PID connected to <InputQueueName>!
DISPLAY QSTATUS('<InputQueueName>') TYPE(HANDLE) APPLTAG PID
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
AMQ8450I: Display queue status details.
   QUEUE(<InputQueueName>)                             TYPE(QUEUE)
   CURDEPTH(0)                             IPPROCS(1)
   MSGAGE( )                               OPPROCS(0)
AMQ8450I: Display queue status details.
   QUEUE(<InputQueueName>)                             TYPE(HANDLE)
   APPLTAG(DataFlowEngine.exe)             PID(14820)
```

</details>

---

## Reading `IPPROCS` Like a Pro

| `CURDEPTH` | `IPPROCS` (Open Readers) | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | `>= 1` | Healthy! ACE (`DataFlowEngine`) is connected and draining messages immediately |
| `> 0` | **`0`** | **Nobody is listening!** Your ACE flow is stopped or pointing to the wrong queue/QMGR |
| Growing | `>= 1` | ACE is slower than incoming load (or rolling back messages!) — check `MSGAGE` & ACE errors |

title: Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) & Alias Queues
shortDescription: Set up a Dead-Letter Queue + Backout Queue to capture poison messages, and create QALIAS shortcuts.
markdownContent:
# Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) & Alias Queues

In production, never leave poison messages stuck looping infinitely on `<InputQueueName>`. Configure a **Backout Queue** (`BOQNAME` + `BOTHRESH`) and a Queue Manager **Dead-Letter Queue (`DEADQ`)**.

---

## 1. Set Up Dead-Letter + Backout Queues (`runmqsc`)

```text
* 1. Create DLQ & register it on the Queue Manager
DEFINE QLOCAL('<DeadLetterQueueName>') DEFPSIST(YES) REPLACE
ALTER QMGR DEADQ('<DeadLetterQueueName>')

* 2. Create Backout Queue for <InputQueueName> poison messages (move after 3 failed retries!)
DEFINE QLOCAL('<BackoutQueueName>') DEFPSIST(YES) REPLACE
ALTER QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') BOQNAME('<BackoutQueueName>') BOTHRESH(3)
```

Now if an ACE flow crashes 3 times on a malformed message, MQ automatically moves that message to `<BackoutQueueName>` so healthy orders keep flowing!

---

## 2. Create a Queue Alias (`DEFINE QALIAS`)

An alias lets an app send to a friendly virtual name without changing code when the target queue changes:

```text
DEFINE QALIAS('<AliasQueueName>') TARGET('<OutputQueueName>') REPLACE
```

---

title: MQ Listeners: Define & Start Port 1414
shortDescription: Open a TCP/IP listening port (default 1414) on your Queue Manager, discover active or custom listener ports, and alter ports safely.
searchableTerms: Forgot Your Port or Listener Name? Check What Is Running
echo DISPLAY LSSTATUS(*) PORT STATUS | runmqsc <QueueManagerName>
markdownContent:
# MQ Listeners: Define & Start Port 1414

By default, a newly created Queue Manager **has no running TCP listener**, causing `MQRC 2538 (HOST_NOT_AVAILABLE)` when remote ACE flows or MQ Explorer try connecting over TCP/IP. **`1414`** is IBM MQ's standard default TCP port, though you can assign any free port (e.g. `1415`, `1420`) when running multiple Queue Managers on the same host.

---

## Define, Auto-Start & Verify Listener (`runmqsc <QueueManagerName>`)

```text
DEFINE LISTENER('<ListenerName>') TRPTYPE(TCP) PORT(1414) CONTROL(QMGR) REPLACE
START LISTENER('<ListenerName>')
DISPLAY LSSTATUS('<ListenerName>')
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
AMQ8626I: IBM MQ listener created.
AMQ8021I: Request to start IBM MQ Listener accepted.
AMQ8631I: Display listener status details.
   LISTENER(<ListenerName>)                  STATUS(RUNNING)
   PORT(1414)
```

</details>

---

> [!TIP]
> Always include **`CONTROL(QMGR)`**! That tells IBM MQ to automatically start and stop `<ListenerName>` every time `strmqm <QueueManagerName>` / `endmqm <QueueManagerName>` runs in the future.

---

## Forgot Your Port or Listener Name? Check What Is Running

If someone changed the port earlier or you don't know `<ListenerName>`, use the **`*` wildcard** inside `runmqsc <QueueManagerName>`:

```text
* 1. Check all CURRENTLY RUNNING listeners and their ports
DISPLAY LSSTATUS(*) PORT STATUS

* 2. Check ALL defined listeners (even if currently STOPPED)
DISPLAY LISTENER(*) PORT CONTROL TRPTYPE
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
AMQ8631I: Display listener status details.
   LISTENER(<ListenerName>)                STATUS(RUNNING)
   PORT(1415)
AMQ8630I: Display listener details.
   LISTENER(<ListenerName>)                CONTROL(QMGR)
   TRPTYPE(TCP)                            PORT(1415)
```

</details>

**Quick alternatives outside `runmqsc`:**
- **One-liner from CMD / Bash:** `echo DISPLAY LSSTATUS(*) PORT STATUS | runmqsc <QueueManagerName>`
- **Windows PowerShell (running process):** `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='runmqlsr.exe'" | Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine` *(then run `netstat -ano | findstr <ProcessId>` if `-p` isn't shown in the command line)*
- **Linux:** `ps -ef | grep runmqlsr`
- **IBM MQ Explorer (GUI):** Expand **Queue Managers -> `<QueueManagerName>` -> Listeners** to see every listener's **Port** and **Status** columns directly.

---

## Change an Existing Listener's Port

Stop the running listener first, update the port with `ALTER LISTENER`, then start it again:

```text
STOP LISTENER('<ListenerName>')
ALTER LISTENER('<ListenerName>') TRPTYPE(TCP) PORT(1414)
START LISTENER('<ListenerName>')
DISPLAY LSSTATUS(*) PORT STATUS
```

- **Queue manager name:** `<QueueManagerName>`

markdownContent:
# Channel Security & CHLAUTH Basics

IBM MQ ships **secure by default**: every remote connection running as an OS administrator/privileged user (and default `SYSTEM.*` channels) gets blocked with **`MQRC 2035 (MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED)`**.

---

## Recommended Setup (Dedicated App User vs. Local Lab)

| Environment | Recommended Fix for `MQRC 2035` |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Staging / Production** | Create a dedicated non-admin OS/LDAP user (`<UserName>`), map it via `SET CHLAUTH`, and enable TLS + user credentials (`mqsisetdbparms`) |
| **Isolated Local Dev Lab Only** | Allow your app channel (`<ChannelName>`) via `SET CHLAUTH` on your sandbox QMGR |

---

## Check What Blocked You First!

Always inspect `AMQERR01.LOG` — MQ explicitly prints **which exact rule** rejected your connection. Then configure a scoped rule in `runmqsc`:

```text
* Allow specific service user '<UserName>' over <ChannelName>
SET CHLAUTH('<ChannelName>') TYPE(USERMAP) CLNTUSER('<UserName>') USERSRC(MAP) MCAUSER('<UserName>') ACTION(ADD)
REFRESH SECURITY(*)
```

And grant `<UserName>` permission on queues via `setmqaut`:
```bash
setmqaut -m <QueueManagerName> -t qmgr -p <UserName> +connect +inq
setmqaut -m <QueueManagerName> -n <InputQueueName> -t queue -p <UserName> +get +browse +inq
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Never disable `CHLAUTH` or `CONNAUTH` on shared or production servers!** Disabling channel auth exposes every queue on port `1414` to unauthenticated administrative access.

---

```bash
amqsput <InputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>
```

```text
Sample AMQSPUT0 end
```

```bash
echo {"orderId": 102, "amount": 99} | amqsput <InputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>
```

# amqsget: Read Messages & Empty a Queue

**`amqsget`** pulls every message off a queue, prints it to your screen, and **removes it permanently** (destructive GET).

---

## Syntax & Example

```bash
amqsget <OutputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```text
Sample AMQSGET0 start
message <{"orderId":101,"status":"PROCESSED"}>
no more messages
Sample AMQSGET0 end
```

</details>

---

> [!WARNING]
> Notice **`amqsget` DESTROYS/CONSUMES the message** from the queue! If you only want to **peek** at a queue without removing messages, use **[amqsbcg](#topic-246)** instead. Also expect a brief ~15-second wait after the last message before it prints `no more messages` and exits.

# MQ Error Logs (AMQERR01.LOG) & Troubleshooting

Whenever IBM MQ throws an unclear failure (`2035`, channel won't start, Queue Manager fails to boot), open **`AMQERR01.LOG`** — always read the **bottom** (newest messages first!).

---

## Where to Find `AMQERR01.LOG`

| OS | Queue Manager Error Log | System-Wide Error Log |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Windows** | `C:\ProgramData\IBM\MQ\qmgrs\<QMGR>\errors\AMQERR01.LOG` | `C:\ProgramData\IBM\MQ\errors\AMQERR01.LOG` |
| **Linux / Container** | `/var/mqm/qmgrs/<QMGR>/errors/AMQERR01.LOG` | `/var/mqm/errors/AMQERR01.LOG` |

*(IBM MQ rotates logs cleanly: `AMQERR01.LOG` is active, `02` and `03` are older rollovers.)*

---

## Quick Tail on Linux / PowerShell

```bash
# Linux: watch the last 30 lines live
tail -n 30 /var/mqm/qmgrs/<QueueManagerName>/errors/AMQERR01.LOG

# Lookup ANY AMQ or 4-digit MQRC error code meaning
mqrc 2059
```


# IBM MQ Commands Cheat Sheet

Replace `<QueueManagerName>` with your Queue Manager name and `<InputQueueName>` / `<OutputQueueName>` with your queue names.

---

## OS Shell Commands (CMD / Bash)

| Task | Command |
| :--- | :--- |
| Check Queue Managers & statuses | `dspmq` |
| Check MQ version | `dspmqver` |
| Create QMGR & set default | `crtmqm -q <QueueManagerName>` |
| Start / Stop QMGR | `strmqm <QueueManagerName>` / `endmqm -w <QueueManagerName>` |
| Delete QMGR | `dltmqm <QueueManagerName>` |
| Open MQSC admin prompt | `runmqsc <QueueManagerName>` |
| Send / Get / Browse test msg | `amqsput <InputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>` / `amqsget <OutputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>` / `amqsbcg <InputQueueName> <QueueManagerName>` |
| Translate MQRC code | `mqrc 2035` |

---

## Inside `runmqsc <QueueManagerName>`

| Task | MQSC Command |
| :--- | :--- |
| Create local queue | `DEFINE QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>') DEFPSIST(YES) MAXDEPTH(50000) REPLACE` |
| List user queues + depth | `DISPLAY QLOCAL(*) WHERE(NAME NS 'SYSTEM.') CURDEPTH` |
| Who has queue open (`PID`)? | `DISPLAY QSTATUS('<InputQueueName>') TYPE(HANDLE) APPLTAG PID` |
| Empty all messages in queue | `CLEAR QLOCAL('<InputQueueName>')` |
| Create & start port 1414 listener | `DEFINE LISTENER('<ListenerName>') TRPTYPE(TCP) PORT(1414) CONTROL(QMGR) REPLACE` + `START LISTENER('<ListenerName>')` |
| Find active listener & port | `DISPLAY LSSTATUS(*) PORT STATUS` |
| List all defined listeners | `DISPLAY LISTENER(*) PORT CONTROL` |
| Change existing listener port | `STOP LISTENER('<ListenerName>')` + `ALTER LISTENER('<ListenerName>') TRPTYPE(TCP) PORT(1414)` + `START LISTENER('<ListenerName>')` |
| Create remote client channel | `DEFINE CHANNEL('<ChannelName>') CHLTYPE(SVRCONN) TRPTYPE(TCP) REPLACE` |
| Exit `runmqsc` | `END` |

markdownContent:
# ODBC vs JDBC in ACE: Which Database Setup Do You Need?

In IBM App Connect Enterprise (ACE), **the node you put on your flow decides whether you set up ODBC or JDBC** to talk to Microsoft SQL Server.

![Diagram showing Compute/Database using OS ODBC DSN vs Mapping/JavaCompute using JDBCProviders Policy to reach SQL Server](/images/ace/diagram-sql-server-odbc-jdbc.svg)

---

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Node You Use | Connection Type Required | Where You Configure Connection | Driver Needed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`Compute` / `Database` / `Filter`** | **ODBC (System DSN)** | OS ODBC (`odbcad32.exe` on Windows, `odbc.ini` on Linux) + node **Data source** property | 64-bit SQL Server ODBC driver (or ACE DataDirect `UKsqls95.so` on Linux) |
| **`Mapping` / `JavaCompute`** | **JDBC (`JDBCProviders` Policy)** | Policy Project (`type=JDBCProviders`) + server `jarsURL` | Microsoft `mssql-jdbc-*.jar` |

---

## Quick Checklist Before Connecting to SQL Server

Make sure **SQL Server itself** allows TCP connections first (especially on a local dev PC where TCP/IP is often **disabled** after install!):

1. Open **SQL Server Configuration Manager** -> **SQL Server Network Configuration -> Protocols for `<INSTANCE>`**.
2. Right-click **TCP/IP** -> **Enable**.
3. Double-click **TCP/IP** -> **IP Addresses** tab -> scroll to **IPAll** -> set **TCP Port = `1433`** (and clear TCP Dynamic Ports).
4. **Restart** the `SQL Server` Windows service.
5. **Verify SQL Server is actually listening on port `1433`:**

```bash
# Windows CMD (check local machine is LISTENING + confirm PID belongs to sqlservr.exe)
netstat -ano | findstr :1433

# Windows PowerShell (check reachability + Firewall from ACE machine)
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <HostName> -Port 1433

# Linux (check listening socket on port 1433)
ss -tlnp | grep :1433
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output When SQL Server Is Listening</summary>

```text
  TCP    0.0.0.0:1433           0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING       4812
  TCP    [::]:1433              [::]:0                 LISTENING       4812
```

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> Using a dynamic **Named Instance** like `<HostName>\<InstanceName>` instead of fixed port `1433`? Make sure the **SQL Server Browser** Windows service is running too — it listens on **UDP port `1434`** to tell ACE which port that instance uses!

> [!TIP]
> If your flow uses **ESQL inside a `Compute` node** (the most common pattern in ACE), follow the **ODBC** path in the next topic! You only need `JDBCProviders` if you query tables inside a **Mapping (`.map`)** or **JavaCompute** node.

---

# Connect ACE to SQL Server on Windows (64-bit ODBC)

On **Windows**, IBM ACE does **not** use text `.ini` files — it reads **System DSNs** directly from the **64-bit** Windows ODBC Data Source Administrator.

---

## Step 1: Make Sure You Have a 64-bit SQL Server ODBC Driver

Check that **ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server** or **ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server** (x64) is installed on Windows. *(If missing, install Microsoft's free "Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server x64".)*

---

## Step 2: Open the **64-bit** ODBC Administrator (Very Important!)

1. Press **Win + R**, type the exact full 64-bit path, and press **Enter**:

```text
C:\Windows\System32\odbcad32.exe
```

*(Never open the 32-bit one inside `SysWOW64` — ACE is a 64-bit process and cannot see 32-bit DSNs!)*

2. Click the **`System DSN`** tab at the top *(do **not** use User DSN — User DSNs fail when ACE runs under a service account or different user!)*.
3. Click **`Add...`**.
4. Select **`ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server`** (or `18`) -> click **`Finish`**.

---

## Step 3: Fill the SQL Server Wizard

| Screen Field | What to Enter | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Name** | Exact DSN name you will put in ACE `Data source` | `<DSN_Name>` |
| **Description** | Short label (optional) | `SQL Server Orders DB` |
| **Server** | Host + port or named instance | `localhost,1433` or `<HostName>\<InstanceName>` |
| **Authentication** | Pick **With SQL Server authentication...** *(recommended for ACE `mqsisetdbparms`)* | Login ID: `<UserName>`, Password: `<Password>` |
| **Change the default database to** | Check this box and select your DB! | `<DatabaseName>` |

---

## Step 4: Test the Data Source Before Clicking OK!

1. Keep clicking **Next** until **Finish**.
2. Click **`Test Data Source...`**.
3. Make sure you see **`TESTS COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!`** before clicking **OK** -> **OK**.

> [!WARNING]
> **Using ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server?** Driver 18 enables TLS encryption (`Encrypt=Yes`) by default. For local dev servers without a trusted CA certificate, pick **Optional** under **Connection Encryption** or check **Trust Server Certificate** in the wizard, otherwise `Test Data Source` fails with an SSL certificate error!

---

# Connect ACE to SQL Server on Linux (`odbc.ini` & `ODBCINI`)

On **Linux and Docker containers**, ACE 12 ships with built-in **DataDirect** drivers inside `<ace-install>/server/ODBC/drivers/lib/`. For Microsoft SQL Server, copy a sample `odbc.ini` and point it to **`UKsqls95.so`**.

---

## Step 1: Create Your `odbc.ini` File

Create `<OdbcIniPath>` (matching your ACE installation folder, e.g., `/opt/ibm/ace-12`):

```ini
[ODBC Data Sources]
<DSN_Name>=DataDirect SQL Server Wire Protocol

[<DSN_Name>]
Driver=/opt/ibm/ace-12/server/ODBC/drivers/lib/UKsqls95.so
Description=DataDirect SQL Server Wire Protocol
Database=<DatabaseName>
HostName=<HostName>
PortNumber=1433
AnsiNPW=1
LoginTimeout=0
QueryTimeout=0
InstallDir=/opt/ibm/ace-12/server/ODBC/drivers
UseCursorLib=0
IANAAppCodePage=4
UNICODE=UTF-8
```

*(Connecting to a SQL Server **named instance** instead of port `1433`? Replace `HostName` and omit `PortNumber`: `HostName=<HostName>\<InstanceName>`.)*

---

## Step 2: Export `ODBCINI` & `ODBCSYSINI`

Before running `mqsicvp`, `mqsistart`, or `IntegrationServer`, tell Linux where your `odbc.ini` lives (add this to your shell profile or container entrypoint after sourcing `mqsiprofile`):

```bash
export ODBCINI=<OdbcIniPath>
export ODBCSYSINI=/opt/ibm/ace-12/server/ODBC/drivers/etc
```

---

## Step 3: Check Permissions on `odbc.ini`

```bash
chmod 644 <OdbcIniPath>
```

> [!TIP]
> IBM provides ready-made template files under `<ace-install>/server/ODBC/unixodbc/` (`odbc.ini` and `odbcinst.ini`). Copy IBM's sample instead of typing driver paths from scratch so you match your exact fixpack directory!

---

# SQL Server Credentials, `mqsicvp` Test, JDBC & Flow Query

Once your Windows System DSN (or Linux `odbc.ini`) works, finish the setup in **4 simple steps**: save credentials -> test with `mqsicvp` -> reload server -> query in your flow.

---

## Step 1: Save SQL Server Credentials in ACE (`mqsisetdbparms`)

### Option A: Using an Integration Node (`<IntegrationNodeName>`)
```bash
mqsisetdbparms <IntegrationNodeName> -n odbc::<DSN_Name> -u <UserName> -p <Password>
mqsireload <IntegrationNodeName>
```

### Option B: Using an Independent Integration Server (`-w`)
```bash
mqsisetdbparms -w <WorkDirPath> -n odbc::<DSN_Name> -u <UserName> -p <Password>
```
*(Restart `IntegrationServer` afterward so it loads the updated credentials!)*

---

## Step 2: Verify the Connection with `mqsicvp`

Never guess inside a running flow — run **`mqsicvp`** in your ACE Console first:

```bash
# Test against Integration Node <IntegrationNodeName>
mqsicvp <IntegrationNodeName> -n <DSN_Name>

# Or test against an Independent Server / explicit DSN + login
mqsicvp -w <WorkDirPath> -n <DSN_Name>
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output When Connected</summary>

```text
BIP8299I: User '<UserName>' from security resource name 'odbc::<DSN_Name>' will be used for connection to datasource '<DSN_Name>'.
BIP8290I: Verification passed for the ODBC environment.
BIP8071I: Successful command completion.
```

</details>

---

## Step 3: Query SQL Server Inside a `Compute` Node

1. Select your **`Compute`** node -> **Properties -> Basic**.
2. Set **Data source = `<DSN_Name>`**.
3. Query using parameterized ESQL **`PASSTHRU`**:

```esql
SET Environment.Db.Row[] = PASSTHRU(
    'SELECT TOP 1 CUSTOMER_NAME, STATUS FROM dbo.<TableName> WHERE ORDER_ID = ?'
    VALUES(InputRoot.JSON.Data.orderId)
);

SET OutputRoot.JSON.Data.customer = COALESCE(Environment.Db.Row[1].CUSTOMER_NAME, 'Not Found');
```

<details data-type="output">
<summary>Expected Output</summary>

```json
{
  "customer": "<CustomerName>"
}
```

</details>

---

## Bonus: Connecting via `Mapping` or `JavaCompute` (`JDBCProviders` Policy)

If you use a **`Mapping`** node or **`JavaCompute`** (`getJDBCType4Connection`), create a Policy (`Type = JDBCProviders`, e.g. `{<PolicyProjectName>}:<JdbcPolicyName>`) instead of ODBC:

```xml
<policies>
  <policy policyType="JDBCProviders" policyName="<JdbcPolicyName>">
    <databaseName><DatabaseName></databaseName>
    <databaseType>Microsoft_SQL_Server</databaseType>
    <type4DriverClassName>com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver</type4DriverClassName>
    <type4DatasourceClassName>com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDataSource</type4DatasourceClassName>
    <connectionUrlFormat>jdbc:sqlserver://[serverName]:[portNumber];databaseName=[databaseName];encrypt=true;trustServerCertificate=true</connectionUrlFormat>
    <serverName>localhost</serverName>
    <portNumber>1433</portNumber>
    <jarsURL><PathToJdbcDriversFolder></jarsURL>
    <securityIdentity><SecurityIdentityName></securityIdentity>
  </policy>
</policies>
```

Then register the matching JDBC login:
```bash
mqsisetdbparms <IntegrationNodeName> -n jdbc::<SecurityIdentityName> -u <UserName> -p <Password>
mqsireload <IntegrationNodeName>
```

---

## Top 5 SQL Server Setup Errors & Fixes

| Symptom / Error | Exact Cause | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Data source name not found` | Created **32-bit** DSN instead of **64-bit** System DSN on Windows | Recreate inside `C:\Windows\System32\odbcad32.exe` -> **System DSN** |
| Works in terminal, fails in flow | Used **User DSN** instead of **System DSN** (or forgot `ODBCINI` on Linux) | Always use **System DSN** on Windows / export `ODBCINI` before `mqsistart` |
| Connection refused / timeout | SQL Server **TCP/IP** protocol disabled, port `1433` blocked, or Browser service off | Check **`netstat -ano \| findstr :1433`** (`LISTENING`) & `Test-NetConnection -Port 1433`; enable TCP/IP `1433` (and **SQL Server Browser** UDP `1434` for named instances) |
| `Login failed for user` / old password | Ran `mqsisetdbparms` while server was running without reloading | Run `mqsireload <IntegrationNodeName>` (or restart Independent `IntegrationServer`) |
| `PKIX` / SSL verify error (ODBC 18 / JDBC) | Self-signed SQL Server cert rejected | Set `TrustServerCertificate=Yes` (ODBC) or `trustServerCertificate=true` (JDBC URL) |

---

markdownContent:
# BIP Codes Reference Directory (By Symptom)

IBM ACE prints a **`BIPxxxx`** message code in the console, Web UI, and logs (`I` = Info/Good, `W` = Warning, `E` = Error). Find your code below grouped by where it happens.

---

## 1. CLI Startup, Command, ODBC & Queue Manager Codes

| Code | Level | Meaning | Exact Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BIP8071I`** | Info | *Successful command completion* | Good! Your command worked |
| **`BIP8096I`** | Info | Node start command accepted *(check status after a few seconds)* | Run `mqsilist <Node>` to confirm servers report `running` |
| **`BIP8290I` / `BIP8299I`** | Info | `mqsicvp` verified ODBC environment & matched `mqsisetdbparms` login | Database ODBC connectivity is healthy |
| **`BIP8018E`** | Error | Node's associated Queue Manager doesn't exist or failed to start | Run `dspmq` & `strmqm <QMGR>`, or verify `-q` name |
| **`BIP8019E`** | Error | Command flag syntax error or missing parameter | Check required `-e`, `-k`, `-m`, `-a` flags |
| **`BIP1990I` / `BIP1991I`** | Info | Independent Integration Server starting / initialized cleanly | Server is ready on its REST/HTTP ports! |
| **`BIP2866I`** | Info | Admin security inactive (normal on default dev servers) | Enable auth in `server.conf.yaml` for shared/prod |

---

## 2. Deployment, BAR & Server Status Codes

| Code | Level | Meaning | Exact Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BIP1284I` / `BIP1285I`** | Info | Integration Server `<IntegrationServerName>` is running / stopped | Expected status report from `mqsilist` / `mqsistop` |
| **`BIP1275I` / `BIP1276I`** | Info | Application / Flow is running / stopped | Resume with `mqsistartmsgflow` if stopped |
| **`BIP1039I` / `BIP1092I`** | Info | BAR deployment started / completed cleanly | Run `mqsilist <Node> -e <Server>` to confirm active flows |
| **`BIP9332I`** | Info | Application created or updated cleanly | Normal `mqsideploy` confirmation |
| **`BIP15201I`** | Info | `ibmint package` built BAR file cleanly | Deploy the generated `.bar` with `mqsideploy` |
| **`BIP4395E`** | Error | Unresolved **Shared Library** dependency during deploy | Deploy the missing Shared Library to the server first! |

---

## 3. Flow Runtime, ESQL, Mapping & Parser Errors

| Code | Level | Meaning | Exact Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BIP5025E`** | Error | **XML/JSON Parser failure** — payload doesn't match node's Message Domain | Verify Input payload matches node domain (`JSON` vs `XMLNSC` vs `BLOB`) |
| **`BIP2521E`** | Error | Runtime ESQL failure (`InputRoot` write attempted or null math/conversion) | Never assign to `InputRoot`; wrap nullable values with `COALESCE()` |
| **`BIP2531E`** | Error | Array index out of range or `0`-based index in ESQL | Check ESQL loops start at `[1]`, not `[0]`! |
| **`BIP2670E`** | Error | `RouteToLabel` couldn't find matching `Label` node | Verify `labelName` spelling matches a `Label` node on canvas |
| **`BIP2677E`** | Error | `MQReply` received a message with empty `MQMD.ReplyToQ` | Ensure requests stamp `ReplyToQ` or use `MQOutput` instead |
| **`BIP2666E` / `BIP2667E`** | Error | MQ node failed connecting or putting/getting queue (`MQRC` embedded!) | Read the `MQRC` 4-digit code inside the text (e.g., `2059`, `2085`, `2035`) |

---

> [!TIP]
> You can inspect **any** BIP error message's full explanation right in your ACE Console by running: `mqsiexplain <BIPNumber>` (for example `mqsiexplain BIP5025`).
